questions.question: When driving on the expressway during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors to see traffic around you.
Drive on the left side of the lane.
Drive faster than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors to see traffic around you.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving skills test, you may drive on an expressway. Keep proper lane position, safe distance from other vehicles, and correct speed. Always check your mirrors and look around you to stay aware of traffic.

questions.question: When walking around your vehicle before driving, what should you look for?
questions.explanation: When you walk around your vehicle, look underneath for fresh leaks of oil, coolant, grease, or fuel. These leaks could mean your vehicle has a safety problem.

questions.question: A cardboard box on the road could:

options.text: Contain something heavy that damages vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Contain something heavy that damages vehicles.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road is dangerous. A cardboard box might look harmless but could hold something heavy or hard that could damage your vehicle.

questions.question: How much water does it take for a vehicle to hydroplane?

options.text: A lot, like a large puddle

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip and slide on water instead of the road. You do not need much water for this to occur.

questions.question: How can you stay alert and avoid getting tired while driving?

options.text: Close the vents and keep air out.

questions.explanation: A hot cab with bad air flow makes you sleepy. Open a window, use the vents, or turn on the air conditioning to keep cool and stay awake.

questions.question: What is the best way to check your lights during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Park near a mirror to see the reflection
Turn on the lights and get out to look at them
Look at the dashboard to see if warning lights appear
Drive in traffic and wait for other drivers to tell you if lights are out

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the lights and get out to look at them
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, turn on your lights and then exit the vehicle to look at them.

questions.question: On a passenger bus, carry-on baggage should be:
questions.explanation: Passengers cannot leave baggage in doorways or aisles. Baggage must be secured so it does not fall, the driver can move freely, passengers can exit quickly in an emergency, and riders are safe from injury.

questions.question: How can you reduce stress while driving?
questions.explanation: Stress leads to aggressive driving, which is unsafe. Calm music can help you relax and stay in control while driving.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, engine belts should be:

options.text: Checked to make sure they are tight
Only inspected if they look frayed

questions.correctAnswerText: Checked to make sure they are tight
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check engine belts for proper tightness and signs of wear.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, you should:
questions.explanation: Always set the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when facing an aggressive driver?
questions.explanation: When facing an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact. Do not speed up to challenge them. Do not react to their angry gestures.

questions.question: Why must drivers inspect their vehicles?

options.text: Federal and state law requires it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Federal and state law requires it.
questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require drivers to inspect their vehicles before driving. This ensures the vehicle is safe to operate.

questions.question: What are escape ramps used for?

options.text: To exit the highway onto a two-lane road.
To safely stop runaway vehicles on steep hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: To safely stop runaway vehicles on steep hills.
questions.explanation: Escape ramps are built on steep downhill areas. They help stop runaway vehicles safely. They have a long bed of loose, soft material and sometimes an uphill slope.

questions.question: When making a tight turn in a commercial vehicle, you should:

options.text: Drive as fast as a regular car.
Not worry about speed, just focus on the road.
Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind you.
questions.explanation: Drivers behind you may not expect a commercial vehicle to turn so slowly. Brake early and slow down gradually to give them warning.

questions.question: Empty trucks stop in shorter distances than fully-loaded trucks.
questions.explanation: Brakes, tires, springs, and shock absorbers work best when the vehicle is fully loaded. Empty trucks need longer distances to stop because they have less weight and less traction.

questions.question: Joggers wearing headphones:

options.text: Are usually aware of their surroundings.
May not be aware of their surroundings.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not be aware of their surroundings.
questions.explanation: Be careful around pedestrians, joggers, and cyclists wearing headphones. They cannot clearly hear traffic and may not know you are there.

questions.question: If a tire fails while driving, you should:

options.text: Stay off the brakes and let the vehicle slow down.
Stop on the road right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes and let the vehicle slow down.
questions.explanation: When a tire fails, grip the steering wheel firmly. Stay off the brakes and let the vehicle slow on its own. Once it slows, brake gently and pull off the road.

questions.question: When a vehicle starts, the coolant temperature should:
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, the coolant temperature should gradually rise to the normal operating range.

questions.question: What affects stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance is affected by driving speed, vehicle weight, and how slippery the road surface is.

questions.question: The shipper is responsible for safe vehicle operation.
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for operating the vehicle safely and delivering the cargo without delay.
